title: Cross-region priming handoff - scratchpad and weekly notes (2027-11-09)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for the cross-region priming handoff run this week. Goal: validate pre-warm recipes + eviction safety for east-asia / eu-west during a staged burst test, capture gotchas for the SRE/Capacity oncall shift. This is intentionally rough — use to seed the playbook update.

Attendees (sync + async comments):
- Marcus Lee (owner)
- Priya Shah (capacity lead)
- Hannah Kim (SRE)
- Oscar Martinez (platform eng)
- Yuki Tanaka (regional ops)

High-level summary:
- Ran staged priming window 2027-11-09 02:00-04:30 UTC across eu-west1 + asia-east1.
- Used "short-prefix" priming (50% of typical session length) + KV cache population from sample workload.
- Observed 6-12% tail latency increase in eu-west at minute 12-18 after traffic ramp — correlated with background rebalancer churn.
- Prewarming succeeded in asia-east under current instance mix (A100x4), but cost overhead increased ~14% compared to baseline due to padding buffer config.

Experiment details (configs used):
- Priming recipe: prefix_ratio=0.5, kv_shard=4, cache_eviction=LRU-ttl(600s)
- Fleet mix: a100-80gb x4 (asia-east1), h100-80gb x2 + a100x4 (eu-west1) mixed pool
- Routing: prefer-low-latency -> fall back to capacity-tier-2 after 45s
- Autoscale policy: aggressive-burst with cooldown 60s for priming window

Observations / data notes:
- eu-west rebalancer triggered 3 times during ramp; each trigger coincided with controller restarts (see logs) -> investigate controller race when nodes join with older cache manifest.
- KV cache hit rate jumped to 72% in asia-east (from 18% cold) after priming; per-token costs dropped in that window.
- Padding buffer at 20% gave stable latency but raised GPU-hour estimate; try dynamic padding (percentile-based) to reduce cost.
- One node in eu-west reported GPU ECC warnings; replaced and flagged for hardware follow-up (ticket INFRA-HW-203).

Risks / failure modes noted:
- Over-priming: unnecessary warm items persisted and caused memory pressure on smaller instance types (h100-80gb).
- Cross-region cache consistency assumptions broken when route fallback fires — transient mismatches in model version cadence.
- Billing spike risk if priming window left on during normal traffic; need automation to gate by signal.

Action items (owner - due):
- Priya: run a simulation with dynamic-padding heuristics and report cost delta by 2027-11-12.
- Hannah: add health-check gating to rebalancer to avoid restart-trigger loops (PR draft) - 2027-11-15.
- Oscar: investigate cache-manifest versioning race and propose safe join handshake (linked PR #4321) - 2027-11-13.
- Yuki: coordinate with east-asia hardware team on ECC findings and slot replacement schedule - 2027-11-11.
- Marcus: draft a short runbook snippet for oncall to toggle priming windows safely (embed in Confluence) - 2027-11-12.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How aggressive can we be with prefix_ratio without hurting quality for real user traffic? Need to test with live-sampled prompts.
- Should padding be fixed per-instance-type or adapt to observed quantiles? Quick A/B to decide.
- Can we gate priming by predicted demand signal (from routing telemetry) rather than wall-clock schedule?

Logs & quick links (bookmark these while triaging):
- Priming dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/priming/priming-2027-11-09
- Rebalancer logs: gs://infra-logs/rebalancer/eu-west/2027-11-09/*.log
- JIRA: INFRA-7821 (priming rebalancer incident), CAP-901 (capacity simulation for dynamic padding)

Meeting notes end - rough minutes.

Misc scratch:
- consider a lightweight "priming toggle" API key for prod -> allow controlled windows per-customer tier.
- add metric: priming_cost_per_successful_session to Console cost view (product ask).

Next sync: quick async check-in Friday 2027-11-12 morning PDT. If blockers appear escalate to oncall via slack:#gpu-ops.

-- Marcus
(quick, messy; will fold into playbook after action items complete)

Action items assigned to investigate dynamic padding, controller restart gating, cache manifest race, and hardware follow-up.
